gaps.explanation: 'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.hint: the uncountable activity of travelling in general
gaps.explanation: 'Travel' is uncountable when it means travelling in general; the other options are countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.
'Who's' is short for 'who is'; 'whose' asks about possession.

gaps.sentence: Many people fell asleep ___ the lecture.
gaps.hint: within the period of an event
gaps.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun (the lecture) and means within that time; 'while' needs a clause with a verb.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
